checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: Both hands and entire sheet visible on wooden table
must.why: Both hands and the whole sheet are in frame in all four frames; the sheet's top corner is near the frame edge at 0.8s.

must.item: Hands bring one half over the other, producing a folded sheet, not abrupt replacement
must.why: The sheet starts as a tilted, crumpled sheet. By 3.2s it is a different shape and orientation. The result has a diagonal crease and wrinkled corners, not a clean half fold.

must.item: Hands press along the crease after folding
must.why: At 5.6s and 7.6s the hands rest on the paper, but nothing shows a pressing motion along the crease. The right hand claws at the edge in the last frame.

must.item: Hands anatomically plausible with convincing contact
must.why: The fingers look plausible in all frames. The right hand in the last frame is slightly clawed. Contact with the paper is only moderately convincing.

must.item: Blue paper remains a single consistent object
must.why: The shape, size and orientation change between frames. A grey or white underside appears, and corners and wrinkles shift. This reads as morphing.

must.item: Eight-second widescreen, one fixed overhead shot, no sound
must.why: The framing is a fixed top-down 16:9 view. The user was told there is no sound, and I cannot verify that.

faults.what: The fold is not a clean fold in half. The paper starts crumpled and tilted, then becomes a different shape with a diagonal crease, so it looks like a morph.
No clear pressing of the crease. The hands mostly rest on the paper.
The paper's shape, wrinkles and corners change inconsistently. It looks crumpled rather than a plain flat sheet.
The right hand looks stiff and clawed in the final frame.

summary: The clip is a fixed overhead shot of two plausible hands and blue paper on a wooden table, but the paper morphs into a diagonally creased, wrinkled shape instead of a clean half fold, and no clear pressing of the crease shows.
